policy: Latest mutually compatible stable releases; release age triggers review, not automatic replacement. Zero CVEs and actual application/release compatibility remain mandatory. Unknown maintenance is not blanket-approved.
scope: Nine installed older Hex packages and @types/trusted-types. Read-only official GitHub REST, Hex and npm metadata plus local lock/usage inspection; no communications, application edits or dependency edits.

remaining_real_concerns: Current upstream maintenance for four packages is unconfirmed. They are not automatically abandoned; they also cannot be described as confirmed maintained.
telemetry_metrics_prometheus_core has accepted project work but release lag; do not imply the installed release contains main-branch fixes.
No age-only forced replacement or infrastructure/authentication migration is justified by this review. Existing strict audits and actual compatibility tests remain independent mandatory gates.

method_limits: No conclusion is based on GitHub stars, a recent parent alone, pushed_at alone, or absence of the archived flag.

Commit samples are at most ten latest default-branch commits, or package-path commits for DefinitelyTyped. Issue/workflow samples are bounded; this is not a prediction of future maintainer responsiveness.
Repository-root and .github security/support paths were checked. Organization-wide inherited default policies were not exhaustively searched; missing files do not imply no security process.
GitHub CI sample conclusions are reported literally, including cancelled, startup_failure and action_required. Passing unrelated repository runs are not package-specific test evidence.

An empty installed-release security_advisories field is a point-in-time registry fact, not a substitute for the coordinators complete unfiltered Hex/npm audits. This investigation did not rerun those audits or Kith tests.
Public license metadata/README declarations are recorded with provenance; automatic GitHub license detection can be null or NOASSERTION despite a declared license.
